title: JC H2 chemistry — organic: mechanisms, synthesis and the arrow language
subject: science

scenes.caption: Alkanes: one CH₂ group apart
scenes.narration: Organic chemistry starts with carbon chains. Methane, ethane, propane and butane form a homologous series: each member adds one CH₂ group, so the whole family shares one general formula.

shape.explain: Methane: the first alkane - one carbon, four hydrogens.
Ethane: two carbons - one CH2 unit longer than methane.
Propane: three carbons - one CH2 longer than ethane.
Butane: four carbons - each member adds one CH2 unit.
The general formula CnH2n+2 covers every alkane.
The CH2 unit is the repeating block of the homologous series.
Methane plus one CH2 unit gives ethane: the series steps up.

steps.text: A homologous series: same family, same general formula, one CH₂ apart.

scenes.caption: Functional groups change the family
scenes.narration: The same three-carbon skeleton can belong to totally different families. Swap in a new functional group and you get a new homologous series with new reactions.

propanoic acid: the acid made by adding -COOH to propane.

scenes.caption: Electrophilic addition to alkenes
scenes.narration: Ethene's pi bond is electron-rich, so it attacks the slightly positive hydrogen of H–Br. The curly arrows trace where each electron pair goes: first the pi pair to H, then the H–Br pair onto bromine.

scenes.caption: SN1: the slow step comes first
scenes.narration: Tertiary halogenoalkanes substitute in two steps. First the C–Br bond breaks on its own — slowly — leaving a planar carbocation. Only then does hydroxide attack, fast. The slow step is the bottleneck: the rate depends on the halogenoalkane alone.

shape.explain: The overall SN1 substitution: (CH3)3CBr plus OH- gives the alcohol.
The central carbon of the tertiary halogenoalkane.
The (CH3)3C- group: three methyl groups crowd the carbon.
The C-Br bond that breaks on its own in step 1.
The bromine atom, about to leave as Br-.
Bromine: the leaving group.

scenes.caption: SN2: one step, backside attack
scenes.narration: Primary halogenoalkanes substitute in a single concerted step. Hydroxide attacks from the back, opposite the C–Br bond, while bromide leaves — all at once through one transition state. Both reactants appear in the rate equation.

scenes.caption: One route, three steps
scenes.narration: Real synthesis chains reactions you already know. Ethene becomes bromoethane by electrophilic addition, then ethanol by nucleophilic substitution, then ethanal by partial oxidation. Each arrow names its reagents — and you can plan the whole route backwards from the target.

shape.explain: Step A: ethene to bromoethane by electrophilic addition.
Reaction type: electrophilic addition.
Step B: bromoethane to ethanol with aqueous NaOH, heated.
Reaction type: nucleophilic substitution.
Step C: ethanol to ethanal by partial oxidation with K2Cr2O7.
Reaction type: partial oxidation - stop before ethanoic acid.
The route marker: this step links into the chain.

shape.text: retrosynthesis: start from the target, work backwards
shape.explain: Retrosynthesis: plan backwards from the target molecule.

steps.text: Plan the route backwards — each arrow is a reaction you know.

scenes.caption: A common mistake: atoms sliding along the arrow
scenes.narration: A common mistake: reading the curly arrow as an atom sliding along it. The arrow never moves atoms: it reads as a path of motion rather than tracking the electrons themselves. It tracks one pair of electrons from where the pair starts to where the pair ends up.

scenes.caption: Organic mechanisms in one page
scenes.narration: Three ideas carry the whole topic: addition is pi electrons attacking an electrophile; substitution splits into SN1's slow carbocation step and SN2's single concerted step; and synthesis is just chaining those reactions — planned backwards from the target.

shape.text: ✓ addition: π electrons attack the electrophile
shape.explain: Takeaway 1: addition is pi electrons attacking the electrophile.
Takeaway 2: SN1 has two steps; the rate depends on the halogenoalkane alone.
Takeaway 3: SN2 has one step; the rate depends on both reactants.

shape.text: ✓ synthesis: chain known reactions, plan backwards
shape.explain: Takeaway 4: chain known reactions and plan backwards from the target.
